title: The Shared Measure
text: The old survey at {city_name} counted water jars and places to rest along the road. Its last entry names {dungeon_name}. A later warden added a question beside it: who will open the door?
landmark_text: The roadside marks belong to that survey. Their spacing measures the help a traveler could expect, rather than the length of a stride.
book_text: A local margin explains the same measure. A filled water jar counts as one interval; a closed door counts as none. The keeper still asks households to leave room for a traveler.
witness_text: My grandparents argued over the numbers, but both left water by the door. The register ends at {dungeon_name}. I wonder who was there to meet the last surveyor.
author: The local archive of {city_name}

event_notes.text: The supper table is clear again. One stool stayed empty until a late traveler arrived. Nobody had to ask for it.
The carter delivered the supplies. Before counting the crates, a neighbor brought them water and a stool.
